## Eight common assumptions, negated

| # | Usual assumption | If it were false, the conditional effect would be |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | Op effects are additive per edge, so an edit's gain does not depend on other edges. | Gains depend on which ops already sit upstream, downstream or in parallel. |
| A2 | Edge 3 = skip is a harmless shortcut that does not change how deep-path edits behave. | Convs on long-path edges 0 and 2 gain more when the residual shortcut exists, because it helps them train. |
| A3 | Pooling penalties are fixed per edge, independent of neighbours. | Pool→pool in series compounds over-smoothing and gives a super-additive penalty. |
| A4 | More conv capacity always helps by roughly the same amount. | Parallel conv branches saturate at the sum nodes, so a second conv adds less. |
| A5 | Skip-connect is neutral wherever it is placed. | Skip→skip in series collapses depth and makes the cell shallow and under-parameterised. |
| A6 | 1x1 and 3x3 convs differ only by a constant amount. | A 1x1→1x1 chain has no spatial receptive field, so the penalty compounds. |
| A7 | The output node's three branches are independent contributors. | When the sibling branches are parameter-free, the remaining branch becomes the bottleneck and conv edits there matter more. |
| A8 | Removing the edge 0→3 shortcut only reduces capacity a little. | Without the shortcut, damage on the remaining paths, such as pooling on edge 5, is amplified. |

The 20 hypotheses below are each built from one of these negations. Every condition is on a different edge from the edit, and no condition setting is used more than twice.
